question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the status of the Council of Ministers? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 72
Article 74
Article 76
Article 78
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 74

Explanation:
Article 74 of the Indian Constitution deals with the status of the Council of Ministers. It provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President, who shall act in accordance with such advice. After the 42nd Amendment (1976), the President is bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers. Article 75 deals with the appointment, tenure, and resignation of ministers. Article 72 relates to the President's pardoning power, Article 76 to the Attorney General, and Article 78 to the duties of the Prime Minister.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What does Article 74(1) state? → There shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President.
☛ What does Article 74(2) relate to? → The advice given by the Council of Ministers shall not be inquired into by any court.
☛ What change did the 42nd Amendment bring to Article 74? → The President is bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers.
☛ What is Article 75 about? → Appointment, tenure, and responsibility of ministers.
☛ What is Article 78 about? → Duties of the Prime Minister to inform the President.
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का कौन सा अनुच्छेद मंत्रिपरिषद की स्थिति से संबंधित है? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 72
अनुच्छेद 74
अनुच्छेद 76
अनुच्छेद 78
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 74

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 74 मंत्रिपरिषद की स्थिति से संबंधित है। यह अनुच्छेद प्रावधान करता है कि राष्ट्रपति को सहायता और सलाह देने के लिए प्रधानमंत्री के नेतृत्व में एक मंत्रिपरिषद होगी, जिसकी सलाह के अनुसार राष्ट्रपति अपने कार्यों का निर्वहन करेगा। 42वें संशोधन (1976) के बाद राष्ट्रपति मंत्रिपरिषद की सलाह से बंधे हैं। अनुच्छेद 75 मंत्रियों की नियुक्ति, पद व त्यागपत्र से संबंधित है। अनुच्छेद 72 राष्ट्रपति की क्षमादान शक्तियों, अनुच्छेद 76 अटॉर्नी जनरल और अनुच्छेद 78 प्रधानमंत्री के कर्तव्यों से संबंधित है।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ अनुच्छेद 74(1) क्या कहता है? → राष्ट्रपति को सहायता व सलाह देने के लिए प्रधानमंत्री के नेतृत्व में मंत्रिपरिषद होगी।
☛ अनुच्छेद 74(2) किससे संबंधित है? → राष्ट्रपति को दी गई सलाह की न्यायिक समीक्षा नहीं की जाएगी।
☛ 42वें संशोधन ने अनुच्छेद 74 में क्या बदलाव किया? → राष्ट्रपति मंत्रिपरिषद की सलाह से बंधा हुआ है।
☛ अनुच्छेद 75 किससे संबंधित है? → मंत्रियों की नियुक्ति, कार्यकाल और उत्तरदायित्व।
☛ अनुच्छेद 78 किससे संबंधित है? → प्रधानमंत्री के राष्ट्रपति को जानकारी देने के कर्तव्य।

question: The President of India is elected by: (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: direct vote of the people
State Governors
members of the Rajya Sabha only
members of the electoral college
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is members of the electoral college

Explanation:
The President of India is elected indirectly by the Electoral College. This body consists of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the states. The election is conducted by single transferable vote through proportional representation. Voting is by secret ballot. The election is governed by Articles 54 and 55 of the Indian Constitution. Nominees of Rajya Sabha and members of Legislative Councils are not part of the Electoral College.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What voting system is used in Presidential election? → Proportional representation by single transferable vote
☛ Which articles deal with Presidential election? → Articles 54 and 55
☛ Who is not included in the Electoral College? → Nominated members of Rajya Sabha and members of Legislative Councils
☛ What is the term of the President? → 5 years
☛ What is the minimum age for President? → 35 years
question_hi: भारत के राष्ट्रपति का चुनाव किसके द्वारा किया जाता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: जनता का प्रत्यक्ष मतदान
राज्यपाल
केवल राज्यसभा के सदस्य
निर्वाचक मंडल के सदस्य
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है निर्वाचक मंडल के सदस्य

Explanation:
भारत के राष्ट्रपति का चुनाव अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से निर्वाचक मंडल द्वारा किया जाता है। यह निर्वाचक मंडल संसद के दोनों सदनों (लोकसभा और राज्यसभा) के निर्वाचित सदस्यों तथा राज्यों की विधानसभाओं के निर्वाचित सदस्यों से मिलकर बनता है। चुनाव एकल संक्रमणीय मत प्रणाली द्वारा आनुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्व के आधार पर होता है। मतदान गुप्त होता है। राष्ट्रपति का चुनाव भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 54 और 55 के अनुसार होता है।

question: Under which Article of the Constitution can the President of India direct that the provisions related to the Public Service Commissions be extended to any Union Territory? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 335
Article 315
Article 323
Article 321
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 321

Explanation:
Article 321 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to direct that the provisions relating to Public Service Commissions be extended to any Union Territory. This article allows the extension of provisions from Articles 315 to 320 to Union Territories. Article 315 deals with the establishment of Public Service Commissions for the Union and states, while Article 321 specifically authorizes the President to expand the powers and functions of these Commissions. Thus, the President can issue directions under Article 321 to apply Public Service Commission provisions to a Union Territory. Other options: Article 335 relates to reservations, Article 315 establishes commissions, and Article 323 governs the administration of Union Territories.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article 321 → Empowers the President to extend Public Service Commission provisions to Union Territories.
☛ Article 315 → Deals with establishment of Public Service Commissions for Union and states.
☛ Article 335 → Concerns reservations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in public services.
☛ Article 323 → Relates to administration and legislature of Union Territories.
☛ President's power → Under Article 321, to apply Public Service Commission provisions to Union Territories.
question_hi: भारत के राष्ट्रपति किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत किसी केंद्र शासित प्रदेश में लोक सेवा आयोगों से संबंधित प्रावधानों का विस्तार करने का निर्देश दे सकते हैं? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 335
अनुच्छेद 315
अनुच्छेद 323
अनुच्छेद 321
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 321

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 321 राष्ट्रपति को यह अधिकार देता है कि वह किसी केंद्र शासित प्रदेश में लोक सेवा आयोगों से संबंधित प्रावधानों को लागू करने का निर्देश दे सके। यह अनुच्छेद अनुच्छेद 315 से 320 तक के प्रावधानों को केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों पर विस्तारित करने की अनुमति देता है। अनुच्छेद 315 संघ और राज्य लोक सेवा आयोगों की स्थापना से संबंधित है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 321 आयोगों की शक्तियों और कार्यों का विस्तार करने की अनुमति देता है। इस प्रकार, राष्ट्रपति किसी केंद्र शासित प्रदेश में लोक सेवा आयोग के गठन या प्रावधानों के विस्तार के लिए अनुच्छेद 321 के तहत निर्देश जारी कर सकते हैं। शेष विकल्प जैसे अनुच्छेद 335 आरक्षण से संबंधित है, अनुच्छेद 315 आयोगों की स्थापना से, और अनुच्छेद 323 केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के प्रशासन से संबंधित है।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ अनुच्छेद 321 → राष्ट्रपति को केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में लोक सेवा आयोगों के प्रावधानों का विस्तार करने का अधिकार देता है।
☛ अनुच्छेद 315 → संघ और राज्य लोक सेवा आयोगों की स्थापना से संबंधित है।
☛ अनुच्छेद 335 → लोक सेवाओं में अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के आरक्षण से संबंधित है।
☛ अनुच्छेद 323 → केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के प्रशासन और विधानमंडल से संबंधित है।
☛ राष्ट्रपति की शक्ति → अनुच्छेद 321 के तहत लोक सेवा आयोगों के प्रावधानों को केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों पर लागू करना।

question: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution states which of the following? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Official languages
Powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats
Validation of certain Acts and Regulations
Forms of oaths or affirmations
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Official languages

Explanation:
The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution lists the official languages of India. It currently includes 22 languages: Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Sindhi, Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali, Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, and Dogri. The Eighth Schedule provides official recognition and provisions for the development of these languages. Other options like powers of Panchayats (Eleventh Schedule), validation of certain Acts (Thirteenth Schedule), and forms of oaths or affirmations (Third Schedule) belong to different schedules.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ How many languages are in the Eighth Schedule? → 22
☛ Latest added languages → Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, and Dogri (2003)
☛ Main purpose of Eighth Schedule → Recognition of official languages
☛ What is in the Eleventh Schedule? → Powers of Panchayats
☛ What is in the Third Schedule? → Forms of oaths or affirmations
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान की आठवीं अनुसूची में निम्नलिखित में से किसका उल्लेख है? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: राजभाषाएँ
पंचायतों की शक्तियाँ, अधिकार और उत्तरदायित्व
कुछ अधिनियमों और विनियमों का सत्यापन
शपथ या प्रतिज्ञान के रूप
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राजभाषाएँ

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की आठवीं अनुसूची में भारत की राजभाषाओं का उल्लेख है। इसमें वर्तमान में 22 भाषाएँ शामिल हैं, जिनमें असमिया, बंगाली, गुजराती, हिंदी, कन्नड़, कश्मीरी, मलयालम, मराठी, उड़िया, पंजाबी, संस्कृत, तमिल, तेलुगु, उर्दू, सिंधी, कोंकणी, मणिपुरी, नेपाली, बोडो, संथाली, मैथिली और डोगरी शामिल हैं। आठवीं अनुसूची इन भाषाओं को आधिकारिक मान्यता प्रदान करती है और इनके विकास का प्रावधान करती है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे पंचायतों की शक्तियाँ (ग्यारहवीं अनुसूची), कुछ अधिनियमों का सत्यापन (तेरहवीं अनुसूची) और शपथ के रूप (तीसरी अनुसूची) अन्य अनुसूचियों से संबंधित हैं।

☛ तीसरी अनुसूची में क्या है? → शपथ या प्रतिज्ञान के रूप

question: According to Article 37 of the Indian Constitution, the provisions contained in the Directive Principles of State Policy are ________. (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: mandatory for citizens
enforceable by any court
only applicable to the union government
non-enforceable by any court
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is non-enforceable by any court

Explanation:
Article 37 states that the Directive Principles of State Policy are not enforceable by any court. This means that courts cannot compel the government to implement them. Unlike Fundamental Rights, which are justiciable, Directive Principles are non-justiciable. Their purpose is to establish social and economic justice and guide the state in policy-making. According to Article 37, these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country, and it is the duty of the state to apply them, but they cannot be challenged in court. This feature is borrowed from the Irish Constitution. The distinction between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles is a key aspect of the Indian Constitution.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which Article makes Directive Principles non-enforceable? → Article 37
☛ From which constitution are Directive Principles borrowed? → Irish Constitution
☛ What is the difference between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles? → FRs are enforceable, DPs are not
☛ What is the purpose of Directive Principles? → To establish social and economic justice
☛ According to Article 37, Directive Principles are fundamental for what? → Governance of the country
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 37 के अनुसार, राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों में निहित प्रावधान ________ हैं। (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: नागरिकों के लिए अनिवार्य
किसी भी न्यायालय द्वारा प्रवर्तनीय
केवल केंद्र सरकार पर लागू
किसी भी न्यायालय द्वारा अप्रवर्तनीय
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है किसी भी न्यायालय द्वारा अप्रवर्तनीय

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 37 स्पष्ट करता है कि राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व किसी भी न्यायालय द्वारा प्रवर्तनीय नहीं हैं, अर्थात् इन्हें अदालत में लागू नहीं किया जा सकता। ये तत्व मौलिक अधिकारों के विपरीत हैं, जो न्यायिक रूप से प्रवर्तनीय होते हैं। नीति निदेशक तत्वों का उद्देश्य सामाजिक-आर्थिक न्याय स्थापित करना और राज्य को नीतियाँ बनाने में मार्गदर्शन करना है। अनुच्छेद 37 के अनुसार, ये तत्व शासन के मूल सिद्धांत हैं और राज्य का कर्तव्य है कि वह इन्हें लागू करे, लेकिन इन्हें न्यायालय में चुनौती नहीं दी जा सकती। यह प्रावधान भारतीय संविधान की आयरिश संविधान से ली गई विशेषता है।

☛ नीति निदेशक तत्वों का उद्देश्य क्या है? → सामाजिक-आर्थिक न्याय स्थापित करना
☛ अनुच्छेद 37 के अनुसार, नीति निदेशक तत्व किसके लिए मौलिक हैं? → शासन के लिए

question: The directive principles are primarily based on which of the following ideologies? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: State Development
National Security
Social Welfare
Individual Rights
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Social Welfare

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy, enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, are primarily based on the ideology of Social Welfare. These principles guide the state to promote social, economic, and political justice for all citizens. Inspired by the Irish Constitution, they aim to establish a socio-economic democracy by improving living standards, ensuring education, health, right to work, and reducing income inequality. The principles draw from Gandhian, Socialist, and Liberal ideologies, all of which emphasize collective welfare over individual rights. They are non-justiciable but serve as a moral compass for the government in policy-making, focusing on the greater good of society.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which country inspired the Directive Principles? → Ireland
☛ What is the main objective of Directive Principles? → Establish social and economic justice
☛ In which part of the Constitution are they mentioned? → Part IV

question: Article 356 deals with which of the following provisions of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 1)

National Emergency
Official Languages
President's Rule
solution:

Explanation:
Article 356 of the Indian Constitution deals with President's Rule, which is imposed when a state government fails to function according to the constitutional framework. President's Rule is also known as State Emergency or Constitutional Emergency. This provision is a key aspect of Centre-State relations in India's federal system.

question: Which of the following was/were NOT mentioned in the Constitution before 1976? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:
Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution in 1976 through the 42nd Amendment. Before this, the Constitution already contained the Preamble, Fundamental Rights, and Directive Principles of State Policy. The 42nd Amendment introduced Part IVA and Article 51A, which list 11 fundamental duties for citizens. These were based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. Fundamental Duties are not legally enforceable but serve as a reminder of citizens' obligations to the nation.

question: The concept of Directive Principles of the Indian constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of which country?  (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: The US
Ireland
France
Spain
solution:

Explanation:

question: The abolition of the Zamindari system is aimed at achieving which Directive Principle of state policy of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Economic and Social Justice
Environmental Protection
International Peace
Promotion of Education
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Economic and Social Justice

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution under Article 39 (b) and (c) directs the state to ensure that the ownership and control of material resources are distributed to serve the common good and that wealth is not concentrated in a few hands. The Zamindari system was an exploitative land tenure system where zamindars collected rent without cultivation. Its abolition aimed to achieve economic and social justice by redistributing land to farmers, reducing inequality, and preventing exploitation. This Directive Principle guides the state to create a just society by eliminating feudal structures and ensuring fair access to resources. The abolition was a key land reform measure to promote equitable development.

question: According to the Indian Constitution, who is considered as the appointing authority of the members of the State Public Service Commissions?  (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Chief Minister of the concerned state
The Governor
The President
Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Governor

Explanation:
According to Article 316 of the Indian Constitution, the Chairman and other members of the State Public Service Commission are appointed by the Governor of the concerned state. The Governor makes these appointments following the rules made by the President. The State Public Service Commission is an independent constitutional body responsible for recruitment to state civil services. The term of office for members is six years or until they attain the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier. The Governor also has the power to remove members, but only on the recommendation of the President. This provision ensures the independence and impartiality of the commission in state-level recruitment.

question: Who's assent is required for the Constitutional Amendment Bill to become an Act? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: The Prime Minister of India
The President of India
Chief Justice of India
The Speaker of Lok Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The President of India

Explanation:
For a Constitutional Amendment Bill to become an Act, the assent of The President of India is required. Under Article 368 of the Constitution, the amendment procedure is laid down. After the bill is passed by both Houses of Parliament with a special majority, it is sent to the President for assent. The President can either give assent or return the bill for reconsideration. If the bill is passed again after reconsideration, the President's assent becomes mandatory. This process ensures the protection of the basic structure of the Constitution. Without the President's assent, no amendment bill can become law.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which Article deals with constitutional amendment? → Article 368
☛ How many times can the President return an amendment bill for reconsideration? → Once
☛ Is President's assent mandatory if a bill is passed after reconsideration? → Yes
☛ What majority is required to pass a constitutional amendment bill? → Special majority
☛ Is there a time limit for President to give assent to a constitutional amendment bill? → No

लोकसभा अध्यक्ष

question: Under which Act was the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) established? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)

Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999
Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992

Explanation:
The Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) was established under Section 15K of the SEBI Act, 1992. It is a statutory body that hears appeals against orders passed by SEBI, IRDAI, and PFRDA. SAT's headquarters is located in Mumbai. The tribunal consists of a Presiding Officer and two members. Appeals against SAT's decisions can only be made to the Supreme Court of India. question: Which court in India is responsible for handling civil cases like property disputes, divorce and consumer problems? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Sessions Court
Civil Court
Criminal Court
Revenue Court
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Civil Court

Explanation:
In India, the Civil Court is responsible for handling civil cases such as property disputes, divorce, contract breaches, and consumer problems. These courts operate under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. The hierarchy of civil courts ranges from the tehsil-level to the Supreme Court. The Sessions Court deals with criminal cases, while the Revenue Court handles land revenue and land disputes. The Supreme Court of India is the highest civil court. Citizens can file petitions in these courts to protect their rights.

question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution does the Supreme Court have the power to grant Special Leave to Appeal? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 143 of the Constitution of India
Article 136 of the Constitution of India
Article 226 of the Constitution of India
Article 124 of the Constitution of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 136 of the Constitution of India

Explanation:
Article 136 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to grant Special Leave to Appeal (Special Leave Petition) from any judgment, decree, determination, sentence or order passed by any court or tribunal in India. This is a special appellate jurisdiction vested in the Supreme Court, allowing it to entertain appeals in its discretion. It is an extraordinary power that ensures justice. Article 143 deals with the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, Article 226 confers writ jurisdiction on High Courts, and Article 124 deals with the establishment of the Supreme Court.

☛ Special Leave Petition (SLP) → Under Article 136

question: The distribution of powers between the Union and the States in terms of the Union List, State List and Concurrent List is under which Schedule of the Indian Constitution?  (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Fifth Scedule
Seventh Schedule
Sixth Schedule
Fourth Schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Seventh Schedule

Explanation:
The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution distributes powers between the Union and the States through three lists: the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. The Union List contains 100 subjects like defense, foreign affairs, and atomic energy, on which only Parliament can legislate. The State List has 61 subjects such as agriculture, police, and local government, on which state legislatures can legislate. The Concurrent List comprises 52 subjects including education, forests, and labor welfare, on which both Union and States can legislate, but Union law prevails in case of conflict. This division reflects the federal structure of India.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ How many lists are in the Seventh Schedule? → Three (Union, State, Concurrent)
☛ Number of subjects in the Union List? → 100
☛ Number of subjects in the State List? → 61
☛ Number of subjects in the Concurrent List? → 52
☛ Which list does education belong to? → Concurrent List

question: According to the Constitution, which body is responsible for creating or abolishing a legislative council in a state? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: The President of India
The Governor of the State
The Supreme Court
The Parliament of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Parliament of India

Explanation:
According to Article 169 of the Indian Constitution, the power to create or abolish a Legislative Council in a state lies with the Parliament. The process begins when the state's Legislative Assembly passes a resolution with a special majority (majority of total members and at least two-thirds of members present and voting). Subsequently, the Parliament enacts a law to give effect to the resolution. Neither the President, the Governor, nor the Supreme Court has any direct role in this matter. This provision reflects the federal balance and parliamentary supremacy in the Indian Constitution.

☛ How many states currently have a Legislative Council? → 6 (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra)

भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 169 के अनुसार, किसी राज्य में विधान परिषद के निर्माण या उन्मूलन का अधिकार संसद को है। इस प्रक्रिया में पहले संबंधित राज्य की विधानसभा एक प्रस्ताव पारित करती है, जिसमें कम से कम बहुमत के दो-तिहाई सदस्यों का समर्थन होना चाहिए। इसके बाद संसद उस प्रस्ताव के अनुसार विधान परिषद बनाने या समाप्त करने के लिए कानून बनाती है। राष्ट्रपति, राज्यपाल या सर्वोच्च न्यायालय का इस प्रक्रिया में कोई सीधा अधिकार नहीं है। यह प्रावधान संघीय ढांचे में राज्यों की स्वायत्तता और संसद की सर्वोच्चता को दर्शाता है।

question: The Right to Privacy was declared a Fundamental Right under which of the following Articles? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 19
Article 14
Article 22
Article 21
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 21

Explanation:
The Right to Privacy was declared a Fundamental Right under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution. This landmark decision was given by a 9-judge bench of the Supreme Court in the Puttaswamy v. Union of India case in 2017. Article 21 protects the right to life and personal liberty. The Court held that privacy is an independent fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution and is an intrinsic part of Article 21. This judgment overruled earlier decisions that had denied privacy the status of a fundamental right.

question: Which of the following words were added in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Socialist and Secular
Republic and Secular
Republic and Socialist
Democratic and Socialist
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Socialist and Secular

Explanation:
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 added the words Socialist, Secular, and Integrity to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution. Originally, the Preamble described India as a Sovereign Democratic Republic. After the amendment, it became a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic. The word Integrity was also added to the phrase "unity of the nation". This amendment was passed during the Emergency period under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. It explicitly declared India as a Socialist and Secular state.

solution_hi:

Explanation:
1976 में 42वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम द्वारा प्रस्तावना में समाजवादी, धर्मनिरपेक्ष और अखंडता शब्द जोड़े गए। इससे पहले प्रस्तावना में संप्रभु लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य था, जो संप्रभु समाजवादी धर्मनिरपेक्ष लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य हो गया। अखंडता भी जोड़ा गया। यह संशोधन इंदिरा गांधी के प्रधानमंत्रित्व काल में आपातकाल के दौरान पारित हुआ। इसने भारत को स्पष्ट रूप से एक समाजवादी और धर्मनिरपेक्ष राज्य घोषित किया।
